In the luteal phase, the uterine lining becomes thinner and thicker and progesterone rises; this is also when mood changes, bloating, depression, and weakness can come before menstruation starts. There can also be pain in the lower abdomen and back, and some people may feel tired or very tired during the cycle.

proposals.answer_english: Pregnancy prevention methods vary in how effective they are and what can result from them. Hormonal methods, such as birth control pills and other hormone-based methods, are very effective when used properly, but possible effects include rash, headache, mood changes, and irregular bleeding. Barrier methods, such as condoms and diaphragms, are effective when used consistently and correctly, but they can be much less effective than hormonal methods; side effects are few, but some people may get a rash or irritation. Long-acting reversible contraceptives (LARCs), such as IUDs and implants, are very effective and do not require close monitoring, but possible effects include irregular bleeding, pimples, or menstrual changes. Permanent methods, such as sterilization, are very effective at preventing pregnancy but are considered irreversible; possible side effects include surgical risks and complications. It is important for adolescents and health workers to discuss the different options so they can understand how each method works, its effects, and how it fits their individual needs.
